title: Revolts Moplah Uprisings
definition: A series of agrarian revolts by the Moplah (Mapilla) Muslim peasantry in the Malabar region of Kerala against the oppressive Hindu Jenmi (landlord) class and the British colonial administration, peaking in 1921.
importanceInUpsc: Essential for understanding the intersection of agrarian distress, anti-colonial struggle, and the complex communal dynamics during the Khilafat-Non-Cooperation Movement era.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Revolts Moplah Uprisings.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Understanding of the Malabar Land Tenure System
